answer: Sybil resistance in autonomous agent systems leverages verifiable stake and cryptographic commitments to ensure that each agent must marble its identity with economic value, making forges prohibitively costly. By binding reputation to a nectar-like economic utility, agents are incentivized to maintain honest behavior, as any attempt to forge identities incurs slashing penalties exceeding potential gains. This creates an equilibrium where Byzantine agents cannot replicate influence without incurring capital losses, thus maintaining consensus integrity.
